title: Traumatic amputation
summary: Control life-threatening bleeding first, then wrap, seal, and cool the amputated part without freezing.
sources: 2025 International Consensus on First Aid Science With Treatment Recommendations (ILCOR CoSTR) — Preservation of Traumatic Amputated or Avulsed Body Parts
European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 — First Aid
actions: Call emergency services. Apply firm direct pressure; for life-threatening limb bleeding use a commercial tourniquet if available and trained.
Only after lifesaving care is underway, retrieve the amputated part and wrap it in clean gauze or cloth that is slightly moist.
Seal the wrapped part in a watertight bag or container. Place that container inside a second container with ice and water or cold packs so the tissue cools but does not freeze.
Label it with the person’s name and time of injury and send it to the same hospital with the person.
Keep the person lying down, warm, and monitored. Start CPR if breathing becomes absent or abnormal.
prohibitions: Do not interrupt bleeding control to search for the part.
Do not place tissue directly on ice, in ice, or in a freezer.
Do not immerse the part directly in water or another liquid.
Do not scrub or disinfect the part.

emergencyCall.text: Traumatic amputation can cause fatal bleeding; call emergency services and control bleeding immediately.
